protocol.description:
This protocol provides a way to create capture sources from outputs and foreign toplevels. These sources can be used by capture protocols such as ext_image_copy_capture_v1 to capture the contents of the source.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by creating a new major version of the extension.

interface.name: ext_image_capture_source_manager_v1
interface.description: This object is a manager which offers requests to create image capture sources from outputs and foreign toplevels.

request.name: create_from_output

description.summary: create a capture source from an output

request.description:
Create an image capture source from a wl_output.
The source represents the contents of the output. The source will be destroyed automatically when the output is destroyed.

request.name: create_from_toplevel

description.summary: create a capture source from a foreign toplevel

request.description:
Create an image capture source from an ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1.
The source represents the contents of the toplevel. The source will be destroyed automatically when the toplevel is destroyed.

request.name: destroy
request.description:
Destroy the manager object.
Other objects created via this interface are unaffected.

interface.name: ext_image_capture_source_v1
interface.description:
This object represents a source that can be captured. It is created from an output or a foreign toplevel.
The source is destroyed when the underlying output or toplevel is destroyed. The client must not use the source after receiving the destroyed event.

event.name: destroyed
event.description:
The underlying output or toplevel has been destroyed. The source is no longer valid and the client must destroy this object.
Any capture sessions using this source will be stopped.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the source object. This does not affect the underlying output or toplevel.
